correctness.rationale: For each length from three to sixteen two independently written programs enumerated all 2^n binary strings by exact integer loops, with one computing triple counts incrementally via a proven update recurrence and the other directly iterating all increasing index triples. The resulting dictionary frequencies give exactly the stated maxima, histograms and two maximizing 16-bit vectors. The length-sixteen frequencies sum to 36649 classes and weighted sum 65536 words, matching the 2019 reported distinct-deck total. The restricted domain avoids the degenerate n<3 case. The proof is exhaustive and finite; no symbolic all-length inference is made. Both checks executed on the actual files to be delivered.

evidence: The full 2019 paper, Sections II–V, computes reachable deck counts and bounds on D_k(n); its tabulated D_3(16)=36649 is consistent but leaves all individual class sizes unspecified.
The 2020 21-page author preprint studies k-equivalence classes but explicit binary classification focuses on k=2; Section 6 identifies k>=3 extensions as natural.
2015 preprint compares input words efficiently, which could be used as a subroutine to form fibers but does not give the claimed finite census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The algorithms for deciding equality or counting distinct spectra would allow the new figures to be calculated with additional enumeration, but they neither state nor mathematically force the exact histogram without the additional result. The theorem is not presented as a new general technique for deck generation.

originality.rationale: The central newly calculated invariant is the worst-case class size and complete class-size distribution of binary 3-binomial equivalence at length sixteen, together with sharp first failure of L_3(n)<=n for n>=3. It is not the already published D_3(16)=36649, not pairwise class testing, and not the known 2-binomial class algorithms. Closest primary texts were inspected and exact scientific implications compared. Residual risk of unindexed enumeration or uninspected expanded journal is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Unindexed private or historical exhaustive fiber enumeration might reproduce this exact n=16 statistic; lack of matching search hits does not establish absolute novelty.
The expanded 2021/2023 journal full text requires access; only its public abstract and table were inspected. It could contain further size-frequency information not visible publicly.
The finite result does not establish any all-length upper or lower growth law for the maximum list size.

value.rationale: The worst-case size of an inverse image of a k-deck observation is a natural exact reconstruction/list-decoding invariant. The minimal nondegenerate length with L_3(n)>n is a sharp structural boundary for linear-list reconstruction of binary three-subsequence observations. At that length, the calculation identifies both extremal observations and every fiber multiplicity rather than simply duplicating the known number of distinct decks. The exact finite boundary and classification are plausibly useful for benchmark reconstruction, ambiguity distributions and finite-list code selection; no broader theorem is claimed.
